decisions.title: A faster or second chat-model vendor in the race
decisions.gain: About 300 to 400 ms on every turn in that hour, which is the difference between missing the target on most turns and meeting it; 100 to 200 ms at the median at other busy times
decisions.basis: measured: the chat model's first token (fastest of eight copies) is about 700 ms at the median between roughly 23:00 and midnight, against 160 to 320 at other hours, on two nights running; a call at 23:14 on 10-12 had 12 of 13 turns over 1200 for that reason alone; on the simulated customer, same build and persona 14 minutes apart (10-16 23:15 and 23:29): first audio p50 655 → 1214 ms, every other stage unchanged, the chat model's first token 656 → 775 at the median and up to 1341
decisions.cost: A new account and key; answer quality with the 13k-character prompt must be checked
decisions.guard: What the assistant says
decisions.needs: A vendor that answers the 13k-character prompt in under about 400 ms at 23:00 (a prompt cache, or a small fast model), with room for a few copies at once; `scripts/phone-brain.sh llm -last-call ~/golive-last-call.json -try ...` measures a candidate with the real prompt
decisions.status: waiting: two routes to Qwen3.8-27B measured on 10-13 at 20:40 and neither is one to add. With the call's own 13,116-character prompt, one request each in rotation, first token at the median: DeepSeek 581 ms, the same model through SiliconFlow (reasoning off) 1548, through OpenRouter (reasoning off) 1048; all 20 of each candidate's were over 550. With a 30-character prompt SiliconFlow is 409 (p90 457), so the long prompt costs it over a second: no sign of a prompt cache in 20 requests with one prefix. Four copies at once on the SiliconFlow account were refused (HTTP 429) on 148 of 160 requests. With reasoning left on, first token is 3 s (SiliconFlow) and 1.3 s (OpenRouter). DeepSeek's eight copies in the same minutes: 365 at the median, 538 at p90. A candidate has to hold the long prompt in a cache, or be fast without one. MiniMax-M3 (the synthesis accounts' own keys, thinking off, 21:04–21:11): the long prompt costs it nothing (first token 748 ms at the median with it, 713 without) and four copies at once were not refused, but it does not beat what a call does now: its first six characters come 920–980 ms in against 705–720 for one DeepSeek copy, copies of it are slow together (fastest of four 732–748), and DeepSeek's eight copies in the same minutes gave a first token at 377. Its OpenAI-shaped endpoint is slower (1063) than chatcompletion_v2; the priority tier bought nothing clear (584 against 666); thinking left on is 1.1–1.4 s with empty answers. The same again at 23:20 to 23:26 on 10-13, in the slow hour, real prompt: one request each, first token at the median: DeepSeek 601 ms, MiniMax-M3 581, SiliconFlow 1676, OpenRouter 1628. Fastest of several at once: DeepSeek's eight 456 and 434 (it was a mild night: 707 the night before), MiniMax-M3's four 381 and 426. M3's first six characters still trail its first token by about 270 ms against DeepSeek's 70, so on the first clause DeepSeek's eight were ahead (about 525 against about 650). Standing: the two Qwen routes are out; MiniMax-M3 is the one candidate in range at that hour, level with DeepSeek on a bad night and behind it on a mild one, and has not been raced inside golive

decisions.title: Speaker focus: a diarizer beside the audio, vetoing answers to other voices
decisions.gain: An answer to a television or a bystander is dropped before it is heard; the transcript can say whose words were whose. Nothing on an ordinary turn: the model is off the critical path.
decisions.basis: Nemotron-3-Diarization on the box's CPU: 127 ms per 345 ms chunk on a short track, ~330 ms (p90 480) in steady state on a 120 s track; a second voice mixed at −8 dB was labelled as its own speaker for 7.2 of 9.1 s. Labels 220–330 ms behind the audio on the first bench sessions.
decisions.cost: Four CPU threads busy during a call; ~700 ms label lag means a veto lands before the first audio only when the answer is not fast; the model is a third-party 100 M-parameter network with its own failure modes
decisions.guard: observe mode first: attributions logged, nothing acted on; veto only once a call shows the labels in time; a down model is a call without focus
decisions.needs: A call with somebody talking in the background; then veto; a recording of a real background-talker situation to anchor the thresholds
decisions.status: observe since 10-15 12:51 (owner: go ahead to implement)

decisions.cost: One extra chat-model round when a tool is called (the model's 稍等 after the running answer); a result delivered over the caller when no gap comes within 1.5 s
decisions.guard: Delivery waits for a gap; a newer request supersedes an older task; a result nobody wants is dropped; the memory block is after the instructions so the prefix cache holds

decisions.title: Only the primary voice counts: whoever picked up, learned from the call by agreement; the diarizer off the decision path
decisions.gain: A show, a bystander or the assistant's own echo cannot cut the answer, open a turn or be answered: every window of the caller's audio is scored against the caller's own voice within ~200 ms, however much the background talks
decisions.basis: The owner's rule (10-15 22:35): target my voice; a second voice is ignored. The 22:29 call: 38 sounds over the answer judged, 1 in time, the diarizer 1–1.2 s behind under continuous speech. Measured on this line's archive: CAM++ cosine similarity of the caller's later utterances to a 2 s enrolment 0.45–0.68, the assistant 0.14–0.21, the show under 0.25; 10 ms a window on the CPU
decisions.cost: The first utterance is unjudged (nothing to compare with until the caller has spoken ~600 ms alone); a second legitimate speaker on the call (a spouse taking over) is ignored until a handover rule exists; a wrong enrolment (the show speaking first) would ignore the caller — the enrolment extends only with utterances the labels call the caller's; a show playing under the caller's voice makes every window a mixture that scores like a stranger (the 23:20 call: four of the caller's answers dropped), so no verdict may act on a mixture: only a span with zero caller voice is another voice's
decisions.guard: veto mode acts, observe mode logs; the caller's own voice joining an ignored utterance takes it up at once; the threshold is a flag (--threshold, 0.35) and the per-window similarity is in the frames for the journal to read; the caller is whoever picked up — learned from up to six of their own utterances by mutual agreement, one bad window outvoted — never a stored voice unless the line names one (focus_profile); the caller is pinned as the primary and an enrolment the next seconds contradict is distrusted
decisions.undo: Set focus_url back to the diarizer (ws://127.0.0.1:8030/v1/audio/diarize?model=nemotron-diar) and focus to observe; the engine is unchanged.
decisions.needs: A call with the show on (the test), then one with a second person in the room; the threshold read off the journal's similarities.
decisions.status: on the box 10-16 10:45 as the general setup (no profile on the line); first call pending

decisions.title: The target moves from p95 1200 to p95 1000 ms: open every answer from the phrase cache, and race the copies on the first clause
decisions.gain: The only lever that beats both vendor tails at once. Cache-opened turns measured 515–831 ms from last sound (n≈20 over three calls) against a ~880 median and a 1045–1160 p95 on today's good calls; with most turns opened that way the chat model's first token and the synthesizer's first audio move off the path of the first audio, and p95 ~900 is in reach. The first-clause race removes the 600–700 ms first clauses outright (−30 to −60 ms at p90)
decisions.basis: journal/RETRO-1000.md: ~1,100 turns on 24 builds. The ordinary turn is ~880 ms of which ~225 is golive's and the rest three vendors' round trips; the pause is not on the path; of ~70 turns over 1200, ~55% were the chat model's first token, ~20% the synthesizer's first audio, ~12% a patience wait, ~5% a long first clause
decisions.cost: The assistant's voice changes: every answer opens with one of a few short acknowledgements (好的，/ 明白，/ 您说的对，/ 这个我帮您看一下，). That is a change to the owner's prompt, so it is the owner's; one line in instructions_append, no build, two calls to measure. The first-clause race is a small change in internal/provider/hedge.go with a test. Neither touches the 23:00 hour (decision 1)
decisions.guard: What the assistant says; the clause list stays short and the owner hears two calls before it stays. The journal's overview counts against 1000 from the deploy that carries `-target 1000`
decisions.undo: yes — `opener: false` in the profile; the race rule is a config
decisions.needs: The owner's yes on the opening clauses and the wording; then `min_silence_ms` 380 → 300 becomes worth 80 ms a turn and is the next lever
decisions.status: taken 10-25 as a test on the owner's say-so (/goal 1000 ms, "do whatever test you need"): the opener is the engine's, not the model's — `opener: true`, `opener_phrases` 好的，/嗯，/明白， in the telephony profile since de62d5f; the first-clause race is built (`llm_hedge_clause_chars`, off: −28 ms at the median on the bench, the p95 within noise at n=20). Bench of 10-25 22:03, 20 turns: first audio p50/p95 380/380 (850/1077 without); the answer's own first word p50 902 / p95 1076 (first_content_ms). Owner still decides the phrases and whether the voice suits.

decisions.title: Bounded follow-up quotation preparation around the newly selected plan
decisions.gain: Prepare likely next changes while the current quote is being spoken, instead of paying another seconds-long pricing request after each selection change.
decisions.basis: On out-mvukudco-7zrb, two prepared quote tasks took 0 ms, while a two-change selection took 3040 ms and readout began 4848 ms after caller speech. All eight startup prequotes were used; active poll interval 500 ms.
decisions.cost: An opt-in follow_selection_max cap of 8 additional new background computations per call is enabled; the existing initial maximum is unchanged. One in-flight authoritative computation may still delay a foreground miss. The local quotesvc pricing workload is preserved.
decisions.guard: Disabled by default. Reuse cache/in-flight keys without spending new budget; no recursive or comparison seeding; preserve pricing versions and caller variables; foreground work has priority at the next serialized API slot. Discard unstarted obsolete generations. Bound tracked calls to 512 per CRM process and skip only extra warming at capacity.
decisions.undo: Set standard.prequote.follow_selection_max to0, or restore the exact prior quote-plans version through the guarded configuration rollback. Preserve later owner edits.
decisions.needs: Reduce remaining model/readout synthesis delay, repeat the quotation workload and collect at least twenty qualifying physical handset responses. Recheck total-only answer scope. Any audio prewarming must preserve authoritative result validation, bounded per-call attempts and shared provider admission.
decisions.status: The bounded follow-selection policy remains enabled at 8 in quote-plans v7 on runtime bbdb7a3. Replay out-mvumm8e2-t8in retained 0/1/1 ms pricing tasks and an ahead-of-demand third quote, but readouts were 1016/1231/1061 ms. The strict gate fails because the second readout exceeds target and only five caller samples were collected. Physical handset latency remains unproven. The separate coverage replay out-mvumqi79-ghis passed its twenty-response server p95 gate at 1188 ms (max1238), without exercising quotation tools. Neither replay measures physical handset playback.

decisions.title: Prepare bounded call-private audio for completed authoritative quotations
decisions.gain: Remove the first readout synthesis wait when an exact validated prefix is already prepared. The preceding replay measured 171–189 ms in this stage; this is an opportunity, not a measured gain.
decisions.basis: On bbdb7a3, out-mvumm8e2-t8in had 0/1/1 ms pricing tasks but readouts of 1016/1231/1061 ms. The slowest quote spent 171 ms after result delivery before first readout output.
decisions.cost: The telephony trial permits four unique attempted syntheses per call. First use also opens one strict-account connection; every physical provider operation is accounted. Poll the authenticated completed-quote snapshot every two seconds, at most 300 times.
decisions.guard: General default zero, validated 0–8. Same-call budget cannot reset across sessions; 1024 retained claims per server lifetime. No new pricing, prompt or VAD change. Exact foreground result text is authoritative; PCM is call-private, complete, bounded and expires with the quote. Optional work shares known finite account admission and yields to foreground; no background hedge/fallback/reconnect.

decisions.needs: Pass full CI and controlled deployment, verify exact profile delta and archives, replay the same quotation scenario, inspect preparation/cache-hit counts and actual readout latency, then obtain physical handset evidence.
